Both the appeal and the cross-objections arise from the judgment and award, dated 10.06.2021,
passed in M.V.C. No.1095/2020 by the V Additional District Judge and Member, Additional Motor Accident Claims Tribunal, Belagavi (for short, 'the Tribunal').
2. The insurance company is before this Court in M.F.A. No.101340/2021 challenging saddling of the liability as well as the quantum of compensation awarded, whereas the claimants are before this Court in M.F.A. Crob. No.100075/2021 praying for enhancement of compensation not being satisfied with the compensation awarded by the Tribunal.
3.

sentences.text: The claimants, who are the wife, child and parents of the deceased Sri. Rakesh Mahadev Rogi,

filed a claim petition under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 (for short, the 'MV Act')
seeking compensation for the MFA NO.101340/2021 C/w accidental death of deceased Sri. Rakesh Mahadev Rogi that took place on 27.12.2019 involving Ashok Leyland Truck bearing registration No.MH-09/CV-4646.
It was stated that Sri. Rakesh Mahadev Rogi was traveling in the said Truck as a Cleaner and due to the accident, he suffered grievous injuries and died on the spot.

It was stated that the deceased was aged 23 years as on the date of the accident, and he was getting daily wage The Manager vs Smt. Kavita W/O Rakesh Rogi on 19 June, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/17760271/
4 Rs.400/- and batta of Rs.100/- per day.
appeared before the Tribunal and filed their separate written statement inter alia denying the entire petition averments.

entities.text: Manager vs Smt. Kavita W/O Rakesh Rogi
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Respondent No.1-owner of the Truck stated that the Truck was insured with respondent No.2-insurance company and the driver of the Truck was having a valid and effective driving licence to drive the Truck.

Respondent No.2-insurer, in its written statement, while admitting the issuance of policy, has stated that its liability is subject to the terms and MFA NO.101340/2021 C/w condition of the insurance policy.

It was also contended that respondent No.1-onwer of the Truck had entrusted the vehicle to a person who did not have a valid and effective driving licence to drive the vehicle and the Truck did not have a valid permit as on the date of the accident.

It was further stated that the deceased Rakesh Mahadev Rogi was traveling in the Truck as a spare driver, who had no valid driving licence as on the date of the accident, and therefore, the deceased was shown to be working as a Cleaner.
The claim in respect of the Cleaner is not covered by the insurance policy as extra premium amount is not paid.
Therefore, the insurer contended that it is not liable to pay or indemnify the insured-respondent No.1.
Thus, the insurer prayed for dismissal of the claim petition.
5. Before the Tribunal, the claimant No.1, the wife of the deceased, examined herself as P.W.1 apart from marking nineteen documents as Exs.P1 to P19.

On behalf of the respondents, two witnesses came to be examined as R.W.1 MFA NO.101340/2021 C/w and R.W.2 apart from marking five documents as Ex.R.1 to Ex.R.5.
6.

The Tribunal, on appreciation of the material evidence on record, awarded total compensation of Rs.22,31,200/- with interest at 6% per annum on the following heads:
 1) Loss of Dependency Rs. 20,41,200/-
 2) Loss of parental consortium Rs. 80,000/-

3 ) Loss of filial consortium Rs. 40,000/-
 4) Loss of spousal consortium Rs. 40,000/-
 5) Loss of Estate Rs. 15,000/-
 6) Funeral expenses Rs. 15,000/-
 TOTAL Rs. 22,31,200/-

While awarding the above compensation, the Tribunal has assessed the income of the deceased notionally at Rs.9,000/- per month, added 40% of the assessed income towards 'future prospects',
deducted 1/4th of the assessed income towards personal expenses of the deceased and applied multiplier '18'.
Heard Sri. G.N.Raichur, learned counsel for the appellant-insurance company as well as Smt.Sunanda P. Patil, learned counsel for the cross-objectors-claimants.
Perused the impugned judgment and award, and the appeal papers.

sentences.text: Learned counsel Smt. Sunanda P.Patil, for cross- objectors/claimants would submit that the notional income of the deceased assessed by the Tribunal at Rs.9,000/- per month is on the lower side, and the Tribunal ought to have assessed the monthly income of the deceased on higher side taking note of the fact that P.W.1 had stated that the deceased was receiving Rs.400/- as daily wage and Rs.100/- batta per day, which would be Rs.15,000/- per month.
Further, the learned counsel would submit that even the Chart prepared by the State Legal Services Authority would indicate the notional income for the accident of the year at Rs.13,250/- per month.
Therefore, she prays for enhancement of the monthly income.

Learned counsel, Sri. G.N.Raichur for the appellant-insurer would submit that the deceased was traveling in the offending Truck not as a Cleaner and there is no legal liability on the insurer to indemnify the insured for the compensation claimed.

Further, the learned counsel would submit that the deceased was traveling in the Truck not as a Cleaner, but as the second/spare driver; if at all, the claimants are entitled for any compensation, they have to file a petition under the provisions of the Employees Compensation Act, 1923 (for short, 'the EC Act') and the petition filed under the MV Act, is not at all maintainable.

Learned counsel referring to Ex.P.6(a), which is the English translation of Inquest Panchanama at Ex.P.6, would submit that Ex.P.6 indicates the deceased as a second driver/badli driver and for the second/spare driver, the policy would not cover the risk of said person.
Learned counsel would submit that, moreover, the deceased had no driving licence to drive the offending vehicle.
It is submitted that inquest MFA NO.101340/2021 C/w panchanama is a document which is to be relied upon to find out as to whether the deceased was traveling in the Truck as a spare driver.
Learned counsel referring to Section 147 of the Act would submit that the Tribunal could not have entertained the claim petition under Section 166 of the MV Act.
Alternatively, he would submit that the Tribunal ought to have calculated the compensation in terms of the provisions of the 'EC Act'.

10. Further, the learned counsel Sri G.N.Raichur would submit that the claimants have not proved the income of the deceased by placing on record any cogent material and, as such, the notional income assessed by the Tribunal at Rs.9,000/- per month itself is on the higher side since the maximum ceiling limit of wages under the EC Act is Rs.8,000/- per month.
Hence, he prays for assessing the notional income of the deceased at Rs.8,000/- per month.
Learned counsel would also submit that the compensation MFA NO.101340/2021 C/w awarded under other heads are in excess.
Therefore, he prays for reduction of the compensation accordingly.

11. Learned counsel for the cross-objectors/claimants, with regard to the contention of the insurer that the deceased was traveling in the Truck not as a Cleaner, submits that respondent No.1-owner of the Truck had employed the deceased as Cleaner and the deceased was working as such.
Learned counsel would further submit that the charge sheet and FIR states that the deceased was traveling as a Cleaner.

She further submitted that insurance policy issued by the respondent No.2 is a "Package Policy"

6 and extra premium of Rs.60/- is paid for PA Cover to paid driver, Cleaners &
Conductors, and apart from that a sum of Rs.50/- is also paid towards legal liability to paid driver and/or Conductor and/or Cleaner.

sentences.text: Therefore, she submits that the deceased, who was traveling as a Cleaner in the Truck, is covered under the policy.

Thus, she prays for MFA NO.101340/2021 C/w allowing the cross-objections filed by the claimants and dismissing the appeal filed by the insurer.
12.

Having heard the learned counsel for the parties and on perusal of the appeal papers, the points that would arise for consideration in this appeal are,
i) Whether the appellant-insurer proves that the deceased was traveling in the offending Truck not as a Cleaner but as a second/spare driver as on the date of the accident?
ii) Whether the cross-objectors/claimants would be entitled for enhanced compensation?

13. The answers to the above points would be in the negative and in the affirmative respectively for the following reasons:
a) The occurrence of accident that took place on 27.12.2019 involving Ashok Leyland Truck bearing registration No.MH-09/CV-4646, and the resultant death MFA NO.101340/2021 C/w of deceased Sri. Rakesh Mahadev Rogi is not disputed in this appeal.

The cross-objectors/claimants are before this Court claiming enhancement of compensation, whereas the insurer is before this Court against saddling of the liability as well as questioning the quantum of compensation.

b) The learned counsel for the appellant-insurer had mainly contended that the deceased was traveling in the offending Truck not as a Cleaner but as the second/badli driver, and further assuming that the deceased was traveling as a Cleaner, the claim petition ought to have been filed under the provisions of the 'EC Act'.
c) To appreciate the above contention, it would be useful to refer to Section 166 and 167 of the 'MV Act'.
Section 166 provides for making an application for compensation arising out of an accident of the nature specified in sub- section (1) of Section 165.
Section 167 provides for MFA NO.101340/2021 C/w options regarding claims for compensation in certain cases.

Section 167 provides that if a claim arises for compensation under the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 and also under the Workmen's Compensation Act, 1923, the person entitled to compensation may, without prejudice to the provisions of Chapter X, claim such compensation under either of those Acts but not under both.

d) In the instant case, it is the case of the claimants that the deceased was traveling in the Truck as a Cleaner, but the same is disputed by the appellant-insurer stating that the deceased was traveling as the second driver/badli driver and that he was not having a valid and effective driving licence as on the date of the accident.
In support of insurer's contention, Ex.P.6(a) is relied upon.
Ex.P.6(a) is the English translation of the inquest panchanama at Ex.P.6.

In the said inquest panchanama, it is The Manager vs Smt. Kavita W/O Rakesh Rogi on 19 June, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/17760271/
7 stated that the deceased was working as the second driver and was driven by one Bajirao MFA NO.101340/2021 C/w Pandurang Nangare.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The purpose of drawing inquest panchanama is different.

The inquest panchanama is done in accordance with Section 174 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973 when any person dies under any suspicious circumstances, i.e. suicide, murder,
accident etc.

In the panchanama, the details of how the dead body was lying and descriptions such as of any mark of injuries found on person of deceased, apparent cause of death or by what weapon or instrument such marks appears to have been inflicted are to be mentioned.
Thus, panchanama helps to find out whether at the first sight of dead body it can be gathered that cause of death is unnatural.
No reliance could be placed on the inquest panchanama to say that the deceased was traveling as second driver.
Moreover, deceased could not be considered as second driver, since according tot he insurer he was not possessing the driving licence.
But, the charge sheet-Ex.P.5 and the FIR-Ex.P.1 would MFA NO.101340/2021 C/w show otherwise.
Ex.P.1(a) and Ex.P.5(a) are the English translation of the said documents.

A perusal of Ex.P.1(a), the translated copy of the FIR,
makes it clear that deceased was working as a Cleaner with respondent No.1, the owner of the offending lorry.
Ex.P.1 is the FIR registered on the basis of the complaint lodged by the father of the deceased and he has categorically stated that the deceased was working as a Cleaner.
Ex.P.5(a), the translated copy of the Charge Sheet, also makes it clear that the deceased was working as a Cleaner.
It is pertinent to look into the evidence of R.W.2, the respondent No.1 herein, who is the owner of the offending Truck.

R.W.2, in her evidence has categorically stated that the deceased Rakesh Mahadev Rogi was working as a Cleaner in the Truck bearing No.MH-09/CV- 4646, but denies payment of wages at Rs.400/- per day and D.A. of Rs.100/- per day.

In the cross-examination,
R.W.2 admits that the deceased was also traveling in the MFA NO.101340/2021 C/w Truck.
The suggestion that the deceased was not working in the Truck was denied by R.W.2.
Ex.R.2 is the copy of insurance policy.
As on the date of the accident, the said policy was in force and the policy was a "Package Policy".

Apart from the premium of Rs.60/- towards PA Cover to paid driver, Cleaners &
Conductors, another sum of Rs.50/- is also paid towards legal liability to paid driver and/or Conductor and /or cleaner.

Further, the limits of liability under the policy is as under:
Limits of Liability : PA cover for owner driver under section III CSI Rs.0.0/-.
(1) Under Section II(1)(i) of the Policy- Death of or bodily injury to any person so far as it is necessary to meet the requirements of the Motor Vehicle Act, 1988.

(b) Under Section II(1)(i) of the Policy-Damage to property other than property belonging to the insured or held in trust or in the custody of control of the insured up to the limited specified - (TPPD1 Sum Insured - Rs.7,50,000/-, TPPD2 Sum Insured - Rs.6,000/-)
From the above, it is clear that extra premium is paid for driver, Cleaner and conductor with regard to PA cover as MFA NO.101340/2021 C/w well as the legal liability.
The above clause also makes it further clear that death of or injury to any person, is covered under this Package Policy.
We are of the considered opinion that the Cleaner is covered under the "Package Policy".

Therefore, the insurer would be liable to pay the compensation for the death of Sri. Rakesh Mahadev The Manager vs Smt. Kavita W/O Rakesh Rogi on 19 June, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/17760271/
8 Rogi, who was working as a Cleaner and who is covered under the policy.

sentences.text:
e) The claimants had the option to claim compensation either under the provisions of the 'MV Act'
or 'EC Act'.
The claimants have chosen to claim compensation under the provisions of the MV Act.
There is no cogent material placed on record to accept the contention of the insurer that the deceased was not working as a Cleaner.

Since this Court has come to the conclusion that the deceased was working as a Cleaner in the Truck and additional premium was also paid to cover the risk of Cleaner, the claim petition under the 'MV Act' is maintainable and the MFA NO.101340/2021 C/w Tribunal is justified in saddling the entire liability on the insurer of the Truck.
f) This Court has come to the conclusion that the deceased was working as a Cleaner with respondent No.1.
The claimants have stated that the deceased was earning Rs.400/- per day and daily batta of Rs.100/-, but the same is denied by respondent No.1, the employer of the deceased.
No material is placed on record to establish the income of the deceased.
In the absence of any cogent material to establish the income, it is for the Tribunal as well as this Court to assess the income notionally.
The Tribunal has assessed the notional income of the deceased at Rs.9,000/- per month.
The assessment of income by the Tribunal is on the lower side.
This Court and Lok Adalat would normally assess the notional income at Rs.13,250/- per month for the accident of the year 2019.

Therefore, taking note of the notional income fixed as per the Chart prepared by the MFA NO.101340/2021 C/w Karnataka State Legal Services Authority, we assess the income of the deceased at Rs.13,250/- per month.
g) The Tribunal has rightly added 40% of the assessed income towards future prospects in terms of National Insurance Company Limited Vs. Pranay Sethi & Others1.

entities.text: National Insurance Company Limited Vs. Pranay Sethi & Others1
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Since the deceased was aged 23 years, the appropriate multiplier would be '18' which is rightly applied by the Tribunal.
Taking note of the number of dependants, 1/4th would have to be deducted towards personal expenses of the deceased which is rightly applied by the Tribunal.

Thus, the claimants would be entitled to a sum of Rs.30,05,100/- [Rs.13,250/- + 40% (future prospects) less 1/4th (deduction) x 12 (months) x 18 (multiplier)] towards 'loss of dependency' as against Rs.20,41,200/- awarded by the Tribunal.

The Tribunal has rightly awarded a sum of Rs.15,000/- each towards 'loss of estate' and funeral expenses, and a sum of Rs.40,000/- each to the claimants, i.e., the wife, child and parents of the deceased, towards loss of spousal, filial and parental consortium.
Hence, the same is not interfered with.

15. Thus, the claimants would be entitled for enhanced compensation on the following heads:
 1) Loss of Dependency Rs. 30,05,100/-
 2) Loss of parental consortium Rs. 80,000/-
 3) Loss of filial consortium Rs. 40,000/-
 4) Loss of spousal consortium Rs. 40,000/-
 5) Loss of Estate Rs. 15,000/-
 6) Funeral expenses Rs. 15,000/-

sentences.text: Thus, the claimants would be entitled to total compensation of Rs.31,95,100/- as against Rs.22,31,200/- awarded by the Tribunal.

16. Hence, we pass the following:
ORDER a) The cross-objection filed by the claimants is allowed in part.
MFA NO.101340/2021 C/w b) The appeal filed by the insurance company is dismissed.
c) The impugned judgment and award of the Tribunal is modified to the extent that the cross- objectors/claimants are entitled to total compensation Rs.31,95,100/- as against Rs.22,31,200/-
awarded by the Tribunal.
d) The enhanced compensation amount will bear interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of claim petition till date of realization.

e) The appellant-Insurance Company shall deposit the enhanced compensation amount with accrued interest before the Tribunal within six weeks from the date of receipt of certified copy of this judgment.
f) Apportionment, deposit and disbursement of the enhanced compensation shall be made as per the award of the Tribunal.
g) Draw modified award accordingly.

MFA NO.101340/2021 C/w Registry to transmit the records, and also the amount deposited, if any,
by the insurance company before this Court to the Tribunal concerned forthwith.
No order as to costs.

opennyai_summary.facts:
filed a claim petition under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 (for short, the 'MV Act')
seeking compensation for the MFA NO.101340/2021 C/w accidental death of deceased Sri. Rakesh Mahadev Rogi that took place on 27.12.2019 involving Ashok Leyland Truck bearing registration No.MH-09/CV-4646.
opennyai_summary.issue:
Having heard the learned counsel for the parties and on perusal of the appeal papers, the points that would arise for consideration in this appeal are,
i) Whether the appellant-insurer proves that the deceased was traveling in the offending Truck not as a Cleaner but as a second/spare driver as on the date of the accident?
ii) Whether the cross-objectors/claimants would be entitled for enhanced compensation?
13. The answers to the above points would be in the negative and in the affirmative respectively for the following reasons:
a) The occurrence of accident that took place on 27.12.2019 involving Ashok Leyland Truck bearing registration No.MH-09/CV-4646, and the resultant death MFA NO.101340/2021 C/w of deceased Sri. Rakesh Mahadev Rogi is not disputed in this appeal.
opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
d) In the instant case, it is the case of the claimants that the deceased was traveling in the Truck as a Cleaner, but the same is disputed by the appellant-insurer stating that the deceased was traveling as the second driver/badli driver and that he was not having a valid and effective driving licence as on the date of the accident.
The inquest panchanama is done in accordance with Section 174 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973 when any person dies under any suspicious circumstances, i.e. suicide, murder,
accident etc.
In the panchanama, the details of how the dead body was lying and descriptions such as of any mark of injuries found on person of deceased, apparent cause of death or by what weapon or instrument such marks appears to have been inflicted are to be mentioned.
No reliance could be placed on the inquest panchanama to say that the deceased was traveling as second driver.
Moreover, deceased could not be considered as second driver, since according tot he insurer he was not possessing the driving licence.
From the above, it is clear that extra premium is paid for driver, Cleaner and conductor with regard to PA cover as MFA NO.101340/2021 C/w well as the legal liability.
We are of the considered opinion that the Cleaner is covered under the "Package Policy".
The claimants have chosen to claim compensation under the provisions of the MV Act.
Since this Court has come to the conclusion that the deceased was working as a Cleaner in the Truck and additional premium was also paid to cover the risk of Cleaner, the claim petition under the 'MV Act' is maintainable and the MFA NO.101340/2021 C/w Tribunal is justified in saddling the entire liability on the insurer of the Truck.
No material is placed on record to establish the income of the deceased.
In the absence of any cogent material to establish the income, it is for the Tribunal as well as this Court to assess the income notionally.
The Tribunal has assessed the notional income of the deceased at Rs.9,000/- per month.
The assessment of income by the Tribunal is on the lower side.
g) The Tribunal has rightly added 40% of the assessed income towards future prospects in terms of National Insurance Company Limited Vs. Pranay Sethi & Others1.
opennyai_summary.decision:
This Court and Lok Adalat would normally assess the notional income at Rs.13,250/- per month for the accident of the year 2019.
Therefore, taking note of the notional income fixed as per the Chart prepared by the MFA NO.101340/2021 C/w Karnataka State Legal Services Authority, we assess the income of the deceased at Rs.13,250/- per month.
Since the deceased was aged 23 years, the appropriate multiplier would be '18' which is rightly applied by the Tribunal.
Taking note of the number of dependants, 1/4th would have to be deducted towards personal expenses of the deceased which is rightly applied by the Tribunal.
Thus, the claimants would be entitled to a sum of Rs.30,05,100/- [Rs.13,250/- + 40% (future prospects) less 1/4th (deduction) x 12 (months) x 18 (multiplier)] towards 'loss of dependency' as against Rs.20,41,200/- awarded by the Tribunal.
AIR 2017 SC 5157 MFA NO.101340/2021 C/w 14.
The Tribunal has rightly awarded a sum of Rs.15,000/- each towards 'loss of estate' and funeral expenses, and a sum of Rs.40,000/- each to the claimants, i.e., the wife, child and parents of the deceased, towards loss of spousal, filial and parental consortium.
Hence, the same is not interfered with.
15. Thus, the claimants would be entitled for enhanced compensation on the following heads:
 1) Loss of Dependency Rs. 30,05,100/-
 2) Loss of parental consortium Rs. 80,000/-
 3) Loss of filial consortium Rs. 40,000/-
 4) Loss of spousal consortium Rs. 40,000/-
 5) Loss of Estate Rs. 15,000/-
 6) Funeral expenses Rs. 15,000/-
TOTAL Rs. 31,95,100/-

9
Thus, the claimants would be entitled to total compensation of Rs.31,95,100/- as against Rs.22,31,200/- awarded by the Tribunal.
16. Hence, we pass the following:
ORDER a) The cross-objection filed by the claimants is allowed in part.
MFA NO.101340/2021 C/w b) The appeal filed by the insurance company is dismissed.
c) The impugned judgment and award of the Tribunal is modified to the extent that the cross- objectors/claimants are entitled to total compensation Rs.31,95,100/- as against Rs.22,31,200/-
awarded by the Tribunal.
d) The enhanced compensation amount will bear interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of claim petition till date of realization.
e) The appellant-Insurance Company shall deposit the enhanced compensation amount with accrued interest before the Tribunal within six weeks from the date of receipt of certified copy of this judgment.
f) Apportionment, deposit and disbursement of the enhanced compensation shall be made as per the award of the Tribunal.
g) Draw modified award accordingly.
MFA NO.101340/2021 C/w Registry to transmit the records, and also the amount deposited, if any,
by the insurance company before this Court to the Tribunal concerned forthwith.
No order as to costs.
